texasBeacon.finding: The actual current Texas incorporation and exceptions rules inspected do not adopt the October 2026 federal beacon exemption for intrastate commerce. The federal exemption itself expressly leaves state intrastate adoption optional. Thus the federal grant alone is not a demonstrated Texas intrastate legal basis. Separate applicable Texas relief or a compliant warning-device arrangement must be established; do not claim a verified carrier-specific Texas approval process or declare all intrastate beacon operation unlawful on this bounded record.
texasBeacon.confidence: High for text and scope of inspected rules; no exhaustive claim about every possible DPS instrument or carrier-specific legal basis.

sources.evidence: VI.D preempts conflicting state laws applicable to interstate commerce for persons operating under the exemption; states may, but need not, adopt the same exemption for intrastate operations. VI.A grants relief only from 49 CFR 392.22(b), 393.25(e), and 393.95(f).
sources.implication: Do not convert federal participation or two Texas endpoints into proof of intrastate state adoption.

evidence.4.11(a): Incorporates 49 CFR Parts 40, 380, 382, 385–387, 390–393, and 395–397 including interpretations as amended through September 1, 2022. All other CFR references in the subchapter also refer to amendments and interpretations issued through September 1, 2022.

evidence.4.11(c)(1)(A): Includes vehicles/combinations with actual gross weight or gross weight rating over 26,000 pounds operating intrastate.
evidence.4.11(c)(3): Adopts the listed Parts and interpretations pertaining to interstate drivers and vehicles except as otherwise excluded.

sources.implication: This is date-bounded incorporation, not automatic adoption of future federal exemption notices. The Texas substitution of terms extends adopted duties to intrastate work; it does not itself make a movement interstate for the federal VI.D preemption test.

sources.evidence: Rule lists state exemptions and exceptions under Transportation Code 644.052–644.054. Exceptions concern specified oil/well machines, cranes, seed cotton, hours/duty records/ELDs, medical standards, agriculture, older rear-end protection, certain trailer brakes, emergency relief, entry-level training, utility service vehicles and registration. No warning-beacon exemption, 392.22(b)/393.25(e)/393.95(f) relief, or blanket prospective adoption of FMCSA exemption notices appears. Latest amendment effective December 11, 2025, 50 TexReg 7924.
sources.implication: No affirmative adoption of this federal beacon exemption in the current Texas exceptions rule. Search-result mirrors retaining the removed English-language exception are stale and were not used as current authority.

sources.evidence: Section 545.452(c) authorizes the Public Safety Commission by rule to exempt automated vehicles from a specific Texas traffic or motor-vehicle law if the exemption will not cause a public-safety risk. Section 545.455(b)(1) requires capability to comply with applicable Texas traffic and motor-vehicle laws, subject to the subchapter.
sources.implication: Statutory authority to make an exemption is not a granted exemption. The relevant public action would need to be identified; the ordinary TxDMV authorization cannot simply be treated as the beacon exemption.

texasBeacon.recommendedPublicWording: The federal grant does not automatically cover intrastate-only work. Its preemption clause leaves intrastate adoption to each state. Texas’s current incorporation rule still references federal amendments through September 1, 2022, and its listed exceptions do not adopt this beacon exemption. Before relying on beacons alone for genuinely intrastate service, obtain the applicable Texas legal basis or require another compliant warning-device arrangement.
